- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.25) and prices are trending down, model often over-anticipates recovery; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid premature upside.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently over-estimates continuation; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for 3–5 days, then allow gradual mean reversion.  
- Model underestimates long-term mean reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7); add 0.5–1.5% bias toward historical average over 18-day window.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal patterns (e.g., 0.5→0.2→0.7), model often misreads momentum; apply lagged sentiment smoothing: forecast = 0.7×prior + 0.3×current sentiment-weighted average.
